Summaries

five sample summaries

[1] He talks about what he learned from playing ping-pong in Japan. In his club, players change partners every five minutes. And play doubles. They do not focus on who wins or loses. Instead they try to make everyone feel like a winner. He also explains the history of ping-pong and how it helped improve relationships between countries. He tells a story about a player who survived a concentration camp because a guard recognized him from ping-pong. Through these experiences, Lyer learned that winning is not the most important thing. The most important thing is enjoying the game and connecting with other people.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          
[2] Pico lyer talked about what ping-pong taught him about life. Every night, he goes to a local health club to play ping-pong. There are a few ping-pong tables, so people make a partner and play doubles. They change their partner every 5 minutes, so they don’t focus on winning. They try to harmonise with each other. After the match, they can feel the winner's emotion whether they won or not. He said that Japan raised their competitive spirit without competition. Also, he said that Japan tends to think that it’s important for many people to feel that they are winners. However, in Western countries like England, ping-pong was considered an aristocratic sport. They played ping-pong with wine cork after the dinner. Also, they were taught that the point of a game was to win. If people concentrate on winning, and they lose, they will be really shocked. However, if people focus on enjoying themselves, they can feel happiness. This logic not only applies for sports games, but also jobs.
[3] Pico Iyer talks about what ping-pong taught him about life. In Japan, people play to enjoy the game together, not just to win. He explains that teamwork and friendship are more important than winning or losing. He learned that we should enjoy the experience and not focus too much on the score.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        
[4] In this TED Talk, Pico Iyer talks about what ping-pong taught him about life. In his health club in Japan, people play doubles and change partners every five minutes. They try hard to win points, but they do not care much about the final score. He says that this way of playing helps everyone enjoy the game. He also talks about the history of ping-pong. Hungary was very strong after World War I, and one point in a game in 1936 lasted more than two hours. Later, a Japanese player named Hiroji Satoh won a gold medal in 1952 with a new type of paddle. Through his experiences in Japan, Iyer learned that winning is not the most important thing. He believes that making other people happy is also important. He compares playing doubles to singing in a choir because everyone works together to make something good. At the end, he explains that being part of something can be more important than winning or losing.                                                                             
[5] In this video, a speaker, Pico, learned about things from Ping-Pong in Japan. He learned that the game's results are not all. He gave examples of some competitions.

Opinions

five sample opinions

[1] I agree with Iyer’s idea that having fun with other people is more important than winning. When people only think about winning, they may feel sad when they lose. I think it is important to enjoy the activity and respect other people. I also like his idea that everyone should have a chance to enjoy the game. However, I do not completely agree with him. I think competition is also important because it gives people a reason to practice harder and improve their skills. For example, when I play sports, trying to win can make me work harder. In my opinion, we should try our best to win, but we should not forget to enjoy playing with others.                                                                                                                                               
[2] I found Iyer’s speech interesting because it made me reconsider the meaning of winning and losing. I especially agree with his idea that cooperation and making others feel included are more important than individual victories. In everyday life, I think we sometimes focus too much on comparing ourselves with others and forget to enjoy the experience itself. However, I do not think competition is always negative. Healthy competition can encourage people to improve themselves and discover their potential. I believe the important thing is to find a balance between competition and cooperation. We should try our best while also respecting and supporting others. To me, true success is not only about achieving personal goals, but also about growing together with the people around us.
[3] I almost agree with his speech because he recognized the Japanese national character exactly even though he is not from Japan. Moreover, he got knowledge about Japanese culture through learning ping-pong, which was surprising for me because it was unique. And also, I have one more surprising thing in his speech. That is, the culture of ping-pong is related to western countries. I didn't know that actually. For example, the origin of ping-pong (the noble started hitting kurk over the table) was such an interesting story.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     
[4] This video was very difficult to understand. I did not expect content from the title, and it used words which I was not familiar with. However, I think that phrase overtaking is not the same as being defeated is good.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         
[5] I agree with his idea that playing together and helping each other grow are more important than simply winning.When I was an elementary school student, I really disliked PE classes because students were often compared with each other.
